decision_reason: A1 already supplies useful intensity, timing, posture and rotation contrasts. The closest unseen pair, sitting and standing, differs only in posture_inclination; the supplied capabilities do not justify manufacturing another stable distinction between these largely static activities. Feeding activities also have close prototypes, but food identity, utensil use and grip are not reliably inferable from the listed capabilities. Add one complementary wrist-motion duty-cycle concept to distinguish sustained wrist activity from movement separated by holds, supporting transfer from writing, typing and drinking from cup to brushing teeth and feeding. Preserve the remaining A1 concepts rather than introducing uncertain fine-grained distinctions. The supplied coverage diagnostics indicate semantic priorities, not expected recognition performance.

attributes.name: motion_intensity
attributes.definition: Overall magnitude and energy of motion within a window, including both linear and rotational components.

attributes.name: cadence
attributes.definition: Rate at which a meaningful periodic motion unit repeats over time. Cadence measures repetitions per unit time, not the total number of repetitions in the recording.

levels.Low: No clear periodic repetition or a slow repetition rate.

attributes.name: smoothness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion changes continuously rather than through sustained rapid fluctuations.

levels.Medium: Moderately smooth motion with some fluctuations.
levels.High: Continuous and smooth motion with little fluctuation.

attributes.name: impulsiveness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion contains short, abrupt, high-magnitude changes or impacts.

levels.Low: Few or no pronounced abrupt peaks.

attributes.name: posture_inclination
attributes.definition: Average gravity-relative inclination of the global load-bearing body configuration within a window, rather than the orientation of an isolated moving limb.

levels.High: Strongly inclined or nearly horizontal relative to gravity.

attributes.name: posture_variability
attributes.definition: Extent to which the global load-bearing body configuration changes relative to gravity within a window, rather than local limb-orientation changes.

attributes.name: rotational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of angular or rotational motion during the activity.

attributes.name: translational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of sustained linear progression or locomotor translation within a window.

levels.High: Prominent sustained translational or locomotor motion.

attributes.name: motion_regularity
attributes.definition: Temporal consistency and predictability of the motion pattern.

levels.Low: Irregular and poorly predictable motion pattern.
levels.Medium: Partly structured motion with moderate variability.

attributes.name: wrist_motion_duty_cycle
attributes.definition: Proportion of time occupied by active wrist movement rather than appreciable quiescent holds, independent of movement amplitude and repetition rate. Brief reversals within ongoing movement are not quiescent holds.

levels.Low: Wrist movement occupies little of the window; quiescence predominates.
levels.Medium: Active wrist movement and appreciable quiescent holds both occupy substantial portions of the window.
levels.High: Active wrist movement occupies most of the window, with few appreciable quiescent holds.

operations.reason: motion_intensity: G3 supports overall acceleration and rotation energy, retaining broad static-versus-active and feeding-versus-vigorous-motion contrasts. Wrist and phone movement can differ, and energetic incidental gestures can obscure the class-level tendency; magnitude alone does not identify the activity.

cadence: G6 supports repetition rate in recurring inertial motion, preserving a transferable distinction between fast brushing and slower feeding cycles. Walking and typing provide different examples of repeated motion. Irregular feeding, short windows and weak wrist expression of finger movement can make the repetition unit ambiguous.

smoothness: G9 supports sustained rapid changes, retaining the existing soup-versus-sandwich contrast without inventing food-specific motion details. Gently transported objects and fluctuating manual actions provide transferable examples. Movement speed and individual technique can alter smoothness, so this is not a reliable food identifier by itself.

impulsiveness: G10 supports isolated abrupt inertial changes, preserving a distinction between generally low-impact unseen activities and seen impact-rich actions. This complements sustained smoothness rather than duplicating it. Object contact, incidental bumps and sensor attachment can create peaks unrelated to the intended activity.

posture_inclination: G1 supports gravity-relative static orientation and retains A1's only sitting-versus-standing distinction, with writing and walking as contextual anchors. However, a user-carried phone has unspecified alignment, the watch measures a limb, and upright sitting is possible; global posture is therefore only conditionally observable. No additional seated-versus-standing discriminator is asserted.

posture_variability: G12 supports changing gravity-relative orientation, retaining the contrast between stable configurations and whole-body repositioning. It supplies seen-supported context for largely stationary unseen activities. Wrist rotation and phone movement within clothing can mimic global posture change, so local orientation variation must not be equated with body reconfiguration.

rotational_motion: G2 supports angular-motion prominence, preserving transfer from drinking from cup and folding clothes to rotation-rich brushing and eating pasta. Watch rotation provides plausible evidence without requiring identification of grip or utensil. Technique, which wrist is instrumented and phone motion can alter the observed prominence.

translational_motion: G13 supports short-window translational-motion evidence, maintaining the useful locomotion-versus-stationary-action contrast across the split. Walking and jogging provide seen progression anchors. Short-window proxies cannot establish sustained displacement unambiguously, and local hand transport or drift can resemble progression; no precise trajectory inference is assumed.

motion_regularity: G11 and G6 support recurrence and temporal consistency, preserving differences between predictable repetition and irregular manual activity. Walking and drinking from cup offer seen anchors for structured motion. Stationarity can also be highly predictable, and variable execution can reduce regularity without changing activity identity.

wrist_motion_duty_cycle: G3, G4 and G11 support the persistence of wrist movement versus appreciable quiescent intervals in watch acceleration and rotation. This adds a temporal-occupancy contrast beyond average intensity, cadence and predictability: brushing can sustain wrist motion, whereas feeding and drinking can alternate transport with holds. Writing and typing supply additional examples of sustained manual engagement, although pauses are possible. The contrast can help close feeding-versus-writing prototypes and contextualize weakly covered brushing; it does not reliably separate chips from sandwich or sitting from standing. Window placement, subtle movements, the uninstrumented active hand and individually variable pauses limit predictability.

semantic_redundancy_review: The ten attributes remain distinct in physical meaning: magnitude, repetition rate, sustained fluctuations, isolated peaks, mean global inclination, global posture change, angular-motion prominence, locomotor progression, temporal predictability and wrist movement occupancy. Duty cycle is not cadence: rapid movements may occur in short bouts. It is not regularity: evenly spaced bouts can have low occupancy. It is not intensity: continuous small movements can have high occupancy but low energy. Some empirical correlation is plausible, but none is assumed. Global posture and sustained translation retain explicit observability limitations. No grip, food identity, absolute hand-to-mouth location, anatomical joint angle or guaranteed extra sitting-versus-standing distinction is introduced.

_meta.validation: Semantic schema and complete A1-to-A2 lineage validated; no feature binding performed.
